# `/sdlc:orchestrate`

Usage:

- `/sdlc:orchestrate` — perform one tick. No arguments.
- `/loop /sdlc:orchestrate` — Claude Code only: repeat on a wall-clock
  cadence; see "Loop cadence" below.

## What this skill does

Run:

```text
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/cli/sdlc orchestrate run --once
```

and report its stdout as your response. That single invocation IS the
tick — T-XRFD moved every dispatch/reconcile/digest decision that used
to live in this skill's prose into the `orchestrate run` op
(`lib/services/orchestrator/`): the `work`/`prs`/`merges` ticks, the
control-plane compatibility gate, per-PR verdict routing, task lease
claiming, and the `.sdlc/orchestrator-log.md` digest line. This skill adds
no logic beyond that one invocation — it does not parse verdicts, dispatch
sub-agents, or branch on exit codes itself.

Run `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/cli/sdlc orchestrate run --help` for the
`--loop`/`--interval` flags. `--once` here is deliberate: the CLI's own
`--interval` sleep loop is for a long-lived foreground process, not a
single skill invocation, so this skill always passes `--once` and leaves
repeat cadence to whatever wraps it (see below).

The op reads `orchestrator:` config (`loops`, `interval_seconds`,
`review.max_rounds`, `review.response_policy`, `router`, `pr_filters`) and
the top-level `notify:` section from the project's `sdlc.yaml` — see
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/conventions/sdlc-yaml.md`.

## The loop's project root

`orchestrate run` works in ONE root: the repository's main checkout by default,
wherever it was launched, so `sdlc.yaml`, `sdlc.local.yaml`, tasks and git all
come from there and the main checkout is never written to (workflows that edit
files run in a worktree). `--root launch` (or `SDLC_LOOP_ROOT=launch`) uses the
folder it was launched in instead; `--root` beats the variable, and an explicit
`--project-root` is used as given in either mode. Any other value exits
`INVALID_INPUT`. Each detached task run receives the loop's root as
`--project-root`.

## Task runs and the loop's own PRs

The `work` tick does not wait for a task. It claims the task's leases, starts
its define/implement/check/judge sequence as a detached run
(`sdlc orchestrate work-run`, recorded under
`.sdlc/orchestrate/work-runs/`) and returns, so up to `limits.executor.implement`
tasks work at once and the `prs`/`merges`/`issues` ticks in the same pass are
not held up. Later ticks read the record: a finished run is reported once, a
run whose process vanished without an outcome is reported as stale
(`stale-slugs=` in the digest, plus a `task.parked` notification) and its
leases are released. With `--once` the runs outlive the invocation.

A run that died leaves its task lease claimed on purpose (the cooldown: a failing
task is not redispatched at once), so the task waits out the lease TTL, up to an
hour. To end that wait, run `sdlc lease task release <task>`: it archives the
lease and drops the ended run's record, so the next tick may claim the task. It
refuses (exit 24) while the run's process or a fresh heartbeat says the holder is
alive; `--force` releases anyway (the process is not stopped, and the forcing is
logged as an `ANOMALY` line; the run then has no claim on its slot or task). Either
way it also clears the dead run's operation and slot leases (never another run's),
and it can be re-run if it stops partway (exit 26) or after an earlier release left
them behind.

A PR on the `task/<basename>` branch of a task the loop ran is always in
scope for the `prs`/`merges`/`issues` ticks, even when
`orchestrator.pr_filters.include_labels` is set and the PR carries none of
those labels; the exclude lists and the draft rule still apply to it. A
human's PR still needs the label.

## Pausing, and acting on one item

`sdlc orchestrate pause|resume|status` is a runtime switch this skill's
own `orchestrate run --once` invocation respects. `sdlc pr route --pr
<n>` and `sdlc task dispatch <basename>` bypass pause entirely — the
manual per-item escape hatch for "handle this one thing now." See
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/conventions/sdlc-yaml.md`'s "Pausing the
orchestrator" / "Manual per-item dispatch" sections for the full
contract (including each command's flags), and `orchestrator.router`'s
doc there for the `live`/`resume`/`fresh` delivery chain `pr route`
and the `prs`/`merges` ticks both use.

## Loop cadence

In Claude Code only, `/loop /sdlc:orchestrate` re-invokes this skill on
the interval configured in `sdlc.yaml`'s `orchestrator.interval_seconds` (default 300s), via
`ScheduleWakeup`. Each iteration is exactly one `--once` pass; the interval
and repeat behavior live in the `/loop` wrapper, not in this skill.

For fast, event-gated wake between `/loop` ticks, pair it with a Monitor
running `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/orchestrate/watch_loop.sh
<project-root>` (see that script's header for its contract) — it wraps the
read-only `sdlc orchestrate watch` pending-work gate and is independent of
this skill's own logic.

## Notes

- `.sdlc/orchestrator-log.md` (gitignored under `.sdlc/*`) is the only
  file this skill's invocation touches, and the `orchestrate run` op owns
  the write.
- This skill never commits; sub-workflows `orchestrate run` dispatches
  (task-work, pr-respond, close-out, pr-update) commit on their own and
  inherit `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/conventions/commit-messages.md`.
- `notify` fires per event, not on a "stuck" threshold: this is a Phase-2
  scope reduction from this skill's own retired prose, which used to fire
  "only when genuinely stuck" (routine blockers did NOT notify). Today
  `notify('task.parked', …)` fires once for EVERY failing step in the `work`
  tick's detached task run (`check`/`judge`/`implement`/…, reported by the run itself) —
  whether a blocking hook parked the branch or the step itself failed — and
  `notify('pr.ci_failed'|'pr.needs_response', …)` fires once a PR's
  `review.max_rounds` cap trips, then REPEATS every subsequent tick for as
  long as that PR stays stuck (no dedup or one-shot suppression), per
  `lib/services/orchestrator/ticks/work.ts` and `ticks/_pr_action.ts`. Each
  channel named by the matching `notify.events.<event>` list (`notify:`'s
  `channels` — `desktop`, `ntfy`, `webhook`) receives every one of these;
  expect more frequent notifications than the old prose skill gave,
  especially on a project with a lot of routine, self-recovering task
  failures or a PR stuck past max_rounds.
